Operating a drone within park boundaries may face law enforcement action and a fine of up to $25,000. Spanning the Alberta-Northwest Territories border, the largest national park in Canada protects a large swath of the Northern Boreal Plains ecosystem, the largest herds of wood bison in the world, vital whooping crane habitat, extraordinary examples of karst and caves, and the Peace-Athabasca Delta. This is the traditional territory of the Dene, Cree, and Métis and is home to many spectacular species, including whooping cranes, bison, wolves, and more. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2023-changes/11_21-feature-change/aurora_feature-640x360.jpg?modified=20231121211426)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/activ/star) ### [Discover the world’s largest Dark Sky Preserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/activ/star) The sky gets plenty dark in the North through fall, winter and spring until, that is, the Milky Way spills across the sky like a starry river. If you’re lucky, the Northern Lights will light up the night sky. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2023-changes/05_23-front-page-changes/AB-JAS-2015-218-640x360.jpg?modified=20230509211257)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/nature/science_nature/fire_management/feu-foret-fire) ### [Fire information and updates](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/nature/science_nature/fire_management/feu-foret-fire) Get up-to-date information on the current fire danger status and wildfire situation. [See all hours](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/visit/heures-hours) ### Social - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/WoodBuffaloNP) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/nahanni-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/nahanni) ### [Nahanni National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/nahanni) Remote granite pinnacles lure top alpinists, wilderness river tripping opportunities attract paddlers, interpreters share cultural and natural history with river trippers, campers and day flight visitors. [![Tehjeh Deé ](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/nattsihchoh-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/naatsihchoh) ### [Nááts'įhch'oh National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/naatsihchoh) In the headwaters of Tehjeh Deé (South Nahanni River) Nááts'įhch'oh National Park Reserve is a place where culture and nature are intertwined. Nááts'įhch'oh offers whitewater paddling and off-the-grid hiking in the Northwest Territories for experienced adventurers. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/thaidene-nene-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene) ### [Thaidene Nëné National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene) Located at the eastern end of Great Slave Lake in the Northwest Territories, Thaidene Nëné National Park Reserve is part of a larger group of protected areas around the East Arm and Artillery Lake regions. _Thaidene Nëné_ means ‘Land of the Ancestors’ in the Dënesųłiné—or Chipewyan—language. | | ### Location 149 McDougal Road Fort Smith NT X0E 0P0 ### Directions All-weather road access is available year-round via the MacKenzie Highway. The MacKenzie Highway links to Highway 5 near Hay River, NT, providing access to the park and Fort Smith. Like many highways in the NT, Highway 5 is mostly hard-packed gravel. There is no all-weather road access to Fort Chipewyan. Depending on conditions, a [winter road](http://www.pc.gc.ca/eng/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/visit/visit1a.aspx) may be open for approximately three months during the winter. This road connects Fort Smith with Fort Chipewyan and Fort McMurray in Alberta. Because of the large distances and potentially dangerous conditions, special precautions are needed for safe travel on the winter road. **Free admission for youth.** Other fees still apply. # Hiking

## Wood Buffalo National Park

**Due to significant changes in the landscape from the 2023 Wildfire season, some hiking trails remain closed.**

This is to ensure visitor safety while we work to complete the required fire rehabilitation to make these areas safe to visit.

Thank you for your understanding and for respecting all area closures. For a full list of what’s open and what’s closed, please visit [https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/securite\_safety/bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/securite_safety/bulletins).

### [Trail rehabilitation](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/activ/randonnee-hiking/rehabilitation)

Learn about trail assessments, rehabilitation planning, and the status of priority trails affected by wildfire.

## Day Hiking

Our trail system offers short, relaxing strolls and scenic, long loops.

### Trails on Highway 5

#### **Wetland Lookout**

Stretch your legs on this short interpretive trail to a lookout, overlooking whooping crane habitat.

#### **Salt Plains Access**

###### Moderate 350 m one way, 700 m return

Make your way down a steep escarpment from the Salt Plains Viewpoint to the Salt Plains. For a hike you won’t forget, search for the spring by the treeline and walk barefoot amongst the salt mounds.

[Map of the Salt Plains Access Trail](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2022-changes/04_21-hiking-page/WBNPSalt-Plains-map--En--Fr.jpg)

### Salt River Day Use Area Trails

[Map of the Salt River Day Use Area Trails](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2022-changes/04_21-hiking-page/WBNPSalt-River-Trails--En--Fr.jpg)

#### **Karstland Trail**

This trail is closed due to a collapsed sinkhole. We’re working on a new route.

###### Easy 780 m loop.

Take a boardwalk through karst and forest to views of sinkholes and access to snake hibernacula.

#### **Salt River Meadows**

###### Moderate 2.2 km loop

Meander side-by-side through wildflower meadows and along a saline stream. This wide trail starts across Pine Lake Road from the Salt River Day Use Area parking lot.

#### **Grosbeak Lake**

###### Moderate 4.0 km loop

This trail through a boulder field at Grosbeak Lake is a “must-see” site in Wood Buffalo National Park. Walk through erosion-sculpted boulders scattered across a white salt pan and to a viewpoint overlooking the lake

#### **Salt Pan Lake**

###### Moderate 7.0 km one-way, 14 km return

Watch for bison as you hike through karst and forest to an escarpment overlooking Salt Pan Lake. To hike a longer loop (15.5 km) combine Benchmark Creek and Salt Pan Lake Trails.

#### **Benchmark Creek**

###### Moderate 8.5 km one way, 17 km return

Travel along a stream, through forest, meadows, and salt flats. Take in views of the Salt River and its tributaries on your way to Grosbeak Lake. To hike a longer loop (15.5 km) combine Benchmark Creek and Salt Pan Lake Trails.

#### **Rainbow Lake**

###### Difficult 6 km one way, 12 km return.

Make your way through wetland, an old forest fire, and towering spruce trees to Rainbow Lake. Watch for signs of bison - wallows, tree rubbings, and tracks - along your way.

### Pine Lake Area Trails

[Map of the Pine Lake Area Trails](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2022-changes/04_21-hiking-page/WBNPPine-Lake-trails-En--Fr.jpg)

#### **Lakeside Trail**

###### Moderate 3.1 km one way, 6.2 km return.

Follow the shoreline through the spruce and aspen forest between Pine Lake Day Use Area and the Kettle Point Group Campsite. Part way, you can also access the Lane Lake Trailhead.

#### **Lane Lake**

###### Moderate 6.5 km one way, 13 km return

Follow a chain of small sinkhole lakes to Lane Lake. Watch for beavers, shorebirds, and loons. Access the trailhead from Kettle Point Road, or make a longer hike by walking the Lakeside Trail from Kettle Point Group Campsite or the Pine Lake Day Use Area.

### Stay safe on the trails

A great hike is a safe hike. Here’s what you need to know to [stay safe](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/Securite_Safety).

# Camping

## Wood Buffalo National Park

### [Backcountry Camping](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/activ/camp/activ2b)

### Pine Lake Campground

Open May (Victoria Day) long weekend until September 30.

Located 60 km south of Fort Smith, Pine Lake Campground is in the heart of the park on the shores of a sinkhole lake. The area has a beautiful sandy beach, cook shelter, playground, and change rooms.

Pine Lake Campground features:

- 18 non-electrical sites, including:

  - three large pull-through sites
  - two wheelchair-accessible sites

- Water (not potable)
- Fire pits with firewood
- Flushable toilets
- Picnic tables
- Bear proof food lockers

**The Pine Lake Campground has both reservable and first come, first served campsites.**

**Reservable Campsites**

Sites #4, #5, #8, #9, #10, #12, #14, P1, P2, and P3 are reservable.

Campsite reservations are made through the Parks Canada Reservation System by phone at 1-877-737-3783 or online at: [Parks Canada reservations](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/reserve).

If you reserve a campsite using the Parks Canada Reservation System please follow these steps when you arrive:

- Check the reservations list at the campground kiosk to confirm your site number.
- Locate your site and set up.
- Leave a scentless item on site while you’re away. BARE campsite policy in effect.

**First come, first served campsites**

Sites #1, #2, #3, #6, #7, #11, #13, #15, #16, #17, #18 are available without a reservation.

If you do not have a campsite reservation follow these steps to register a first come, first served campsite when you arrive.

- Choose any vacant **first come, first served site** (these sites don’t have a reserved sign on them) or choose a reserved site that has an “ **available one night only**” sign on the post.
- Complete a self-registration permit found at the campground kiosk.
- Place payment in the envelope, payment options include cash or credit card, tear off the stub and deposit into the payment vault.
- Display the stub on the campsite post.
- Leave a scentless item on site while you’re away. BARE campsite policy in effect.


### Kettle Point Group Campsite

Reserve your stay at Kettle Point using the Parks Canada Reservation Service.

[Reservations launch  January 21nd at 8 a.m. MT](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/reserve).

Open May (Victoria Day) long weekend until September 30.

Located on Pine Lake, Kettle Point Group Campsite features a large, wheelchair accessible log shelter with a wood stove, picnic tables, and lots of space to store your gear.

This campsite is available for group bookings (minimum group size 8; maximum group size 50) and includes:

- Large grassy area for tenting
- Semi-private beach
- Fire circle
- Firewood
- Picnic tables
- Flushable toilet
- Playground
- Non-potable water is available at the Pine Lake Campground. Water from Pine Lake must be filtered or treated before drinking.
